  • Iran / Campaign: Trump announced a second 10-day pause on Iran energy strikes (deadline Apr 6, 2026 8 PM ET), citing an Iranian request; Iran denies direct talks. First pause was previously violated by strikes. Exchanges of fire and mutual accusations continue. Pakistan is mediating.
  • Strait of Hormuz & shipping: Iran allows passage for Russia, India, China while blocking others. US, Iran and Oman still dispute Hormuz deal details.
  • Airspace & flights: Regional airports reported closed: Iran, Israel, Iraq, Syria, Lebanon, Jordan. Flight trackers show sporadic military flights in the region.
  • International military moves: Russian air defenses reported shooting down two drones heading toward Moscow (TASS). No major Western troop deployments reported in last 6 hours.
  • Good News: Air defenses intercepted drones near Moscow. IDF confirmed high-value militant removals.
  • Threat assessment: Escalating.

48.en:
Situation Report — Day 27

  • Active strikes & sirens: Israeli/US airstrikes on Iranian targets continue. Iran, Hezbollah and Hamas missile/rocket strikes into Israel ongoing daily.
  • Pause / negotiations: Trump announced a 2nd pause on Iran energy strikes (10 days — expires Apr 6, 2026, 8 PM ET). US says talks “going very well.” Iran denies direct talks. First pause (5 days, Mar 23) was violated by US/Israeli strikes on Isfahan and Khorramshahr.
  • Mediation: Pakistan actively mediating between Washington and Tehran.
  • Strait of Hormuz: Iran allows passage for friendly states (Russia, India, China); blocks others. That creates split in global shipping and allies' access.
  • Northern Border (Lebanon/Hezbollah): Daily Hezbollah activity. Israel-Lebanon framework links ceasefire to Hezbollah disarmament; Hezbollah rejects the deal. IDF told to prepare for extended stay in Lebanon; strikes reported in south Lebanon after the framework announcement.
  • Gaza & southern front: IDF strikes continue in Gaza; reported civilian casualties and displacement tent hits. Israeli operations include targeted strikes on senior militant figures (e.g., nephew of former Hamas leader).
  • Airspace & transport: Major regional airports closed (Iran, Israel, Iraq, Syria, Lebanon, Jordan). Commercial traffic reduced; strategic airlift constrained.
  • Tactical context: This is the 2nd formal pause — credibility weakened after the first was breached. Iran’s selective Hormuz openness signals strategic bargaining and pressure on global partners.
  • 🟢 Good News: International mediation (Pakistan) and a 10-day pause offer a diplomatic window.
  • Threat assessment: Escalating — high risk of renewed strikes if pauses break or Hezbollah opens a broader front.
